selectedDefects.issueTitle: Can't view source file if no line number is specified
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the trigger is a selection in the catalog list followed by the 'Code occurrences' context-menu item, so it exercises wx popup-menu dispatch off a list selection and then the creation of a second wxGTK top level window (FileViewer, a wxFrame that wxGTK realizes as a GtkWindow). The observable is what that new frame contains: on the affected revision a reference of the form 'src/main.gd' with no ':line' suffix makes wxString::BeforeLast(':') return empty and the frame shows the 'Source code not found' message, on the fixed revision the same frame shows the file's text. Both states are readable through AT-SPI as static text or a text area inside a newly appeared top-level frame, so the adapter is proving window appearance plus text readout, not an internal value

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Greek Letters panel is always ON at start
selectedDefects.whySuitable: this is a wxConfig round trip across an application lifecycle expressed through wxAUI. The affected revision hard-codes Show(true) on the 'greek' wxAuiPaneInfo while constructing the frame, so the persisted layout is overridden on every start. The trigger is: uncheck 'Greek Letters' in the View menu, quit, start again. Two observables, both native at the wxGTK layer: the pane itself, which wxAUI realizes as a real child window inside the frame carrying the 'Greek Letters' caption and a grid of buttons that AT-SPI enumerates as push buttons, and the check state of the corresponding wxMenuItem, which wxGTK maps to a GtkCheckMenuItem and AT-SPI reports as a checked toggle. The defect is the disagreement between those two, which is precisely a wx adapter question rather than an application-internal one

selectedDefects.issueTitle: [Bug]: Trying to close find panel on Diff View closes the Diff View itself
selectedDefects.whySuitable: two wx event-routing defects in one flow, and both are observable as window lifetime. The find bar registered its close tool under wxID_CLOSE, so the toolbar command reached the diff frame's own close handler, and clDiffFrame::OnCharHook closed the whole frame on WXK_ESCAPE without asking whether the find bar held focus. The trigger is: open the diff view, open the find bar, press Escape or click the find bar's close tool. The observable is whether the diff top-level window still exists afterwards, which AT-SPI reports directly as the presence or absence of a frame in the application's accessible tree, with the find bar's entry as a second, finer observable. That exercises the wx adapter's keyboard dispatch through wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK and its toolbar command-id routing rather than any application-internal state

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Set left/right selection boundary dialogs cannot display positions in any of the bar formats
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the trigger is an accelerator ('[' or ']') that opens a modal TimeDialog, which derives from wxDialogWrapper and is a real GtkDialog at runtime, so the flow exercises wx accelerator dispatch plus dialog modality: the adapter must observe that a modal top-level appeared, that it holds the parent frame, and that it dismisses cleanly. The behavioural difference is in the dialog's numeric control context, which the affected build constructs from a bare sample rate and the fixed build constructs from the project. The stable observable is the context menu that the numeric field pops up: it is an ordinary wxMenu, realized as a GtkMenu whose item labels AT-SPI enumerates, and on the affected build the bar:beat entries the user is looking for are absent from that list while on the fixed build they are present. That keeps the assertion on a native wx construct rather than on a custom-drawn field

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Aegisub crashes immediately after selecting any language from the end of the list
selectedDefects.whySuitable: a wx menu id-range defect: the spell-checker language submenu is a wxMenu built over a reserved block of command ids that only covered 100 entries, so choosing an item past the hundredth dispatched an id outside the backing vector and the process died. The trigger is pure menu interaction, which is the most native thing a wxGTK adapter can drive: open the context menu on the subtitle grid, walk into 'Spell checker language', activate an item beyond position 100. AT-SPI enumerates that submenu's items directly, so the adapter can both count the items and select a specific one by index, and the observable is coarse and unambiguous: the application's accessible tree disappears because the process aborted on the affected build and survives with the chosen language recorded in config on the fixed build

blockers.detail: this gate is qualification only and no Linux build of any wxWidgets subject was run, so buildQualified is null throughout. Every selected defect still needs a two-revision build before S3. wxGTK subjects are source builds against system wx, which is a different risk profile from the electron target where the packaging step was already proven

audacity-time-dialog-format-4568 relies on Audacity's NumericTextCtrl, which is custom drawn rather than a wxTextCtrl. Its accessibility support is guarded by wxUSE_ACCESSIBILITY, which is a Windows path in practice, so the field's text may not be readable through AT-SPI on wxGTK. The plan asserts on the numeric control's context menu labels instead, but that substitution has not been executed and could still fail

codelite-findbar-escape-3071 was reported from macOS. The wxID_CLOSE collision and the wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK handler are platform independent in the diff, but no Linux observation of the affected behaviour exists yet

aegisub-spell-language-131 only fires when the runtime environment offers more than 100 spell-checker languages, which is a property of the image rather than of the application. If the image cannot be provisioned that way, this defect must be dropped and a replacement selected

several strong wxWidgets applications commit fixes directly to trunk with no pull request, so the merged-PR-with-linked-issue recipe finds few candidates: 6 for poedit, 8 for wxmaxima and 2 for Aegisub across their full merged histories. Audacity is the only subject with a deep pool, and only on its 3.3.x revisions, since master is now Qt6. If more than two of the five selected defects fail, replacements will have to come from plain commits that cite an issue rather than from pull requests
